name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen73
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After |change_1m_bps| > 2, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After |change_5m_bps| > 8, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The stronger the recent move, the stronger the reversion tendency.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

THE CRITICAL RECALIBRATION: CRYPTO MOVES ARE ENORMOUS

The primary failure mode is quoting spreads FAR too narrow. Analysis of real outcomes shows:
- Spreads under 10 bps fail almost always
- Even "quiet" conditions routinely produce 5-10 bps moves
- Active conditions produce 15-40 bps moves
- Extreme conditions produce 30-80 bps moves

These are NOT confidence intervals. Half_width is the literal range that must contain the next print to avoid getting run over.

THE CORE CALIBRATION ALGORITHM

Step 1: Identify the volatility regime from |change_5m_bps|:
- |change_5m_bps| ≤ 3: baseline volatility
- |change_5m_bps| 3-8: mild volatility
- |change_5m_bps| 8-15: moderate volatility
- |change_5m_bps| 15-30: elevated volatility
- |change_5m_bps| 30-60: high volatility
- |change_5m_bps| > 60: extreme volatility

Step 2: Set BASE half_width from regime:
- Baseline: 22 bps
- Mild: 28 bps
- Moderate: 38 bps
- Elevated: 50 bps
- High: 65 bps
- Extreme: 90 bps

Step 3: Add adjustments (all additive):

TIME-OF-DAY ADJUSTMENTS:
- 0:00-2:00 UTC (Asian transition): +10 bps
- 3:00-5:00 UTC (quiet hours): +5 bps
- 6:00-9:00 UTC (European open): +9 bps
- 12:00-15:00 UTC (US open, especially 13:30-14:30): +15 bps
- 18:00-19:00 UTC (European close): +7 bps
- 21:00-23:00 UTC (US close/Asian overlap): +9 bps
- Other hours: +0 bps

FUNDING PROXIMITY ADJUSTMENTS:
- >360 minutes: +0 bps
- 240-360 minutes: +5 bps
- 120-240 minutes: +10 bps
- 60-120 minutes: +18 bps
- 20-60 minutes: +28 bps
- <20 minutes: +45 bps

TAPE EXTREMITY ADJUSTMENTS (last bar only):
- taker_buy_share > 0.85 or < 0.15: +15 bps
- taker_buy_share > 0.80 or < 0.20: +10 bps
- taker_buy_share > 0.75 or < 0.25: +6 bps
- Sustained imbalance (3+ bars > 0.70 or < 0.30): +9 bps
- Tape whipsaw (consecutive bars flipping >0.75 to <0.25 or vice versa): +18 bps

RECENT LARGE MOVE ADJUSTMENTS:
- |change_1m_bps| > 15: +12 bps (reversion expected but path volatile)
- |change_1m_bps| > 25: +22 bps
- |change_5m_bps| > 30: +15 bps (extreme regime already sets high base, add for path uncertainty)
- Multiple bars in last 5 minutes each >8 bps: +10 bps

VOLUME ADJUSTMENTS (if available):
- Volume >150% typical for hour: +11 bps
- Volume >250% typical: +20 bps
- Volume <40% typical (thin book): +10 bps

Step 4: Calculate final half_width = BASE + all applicable adjustments

NEVER QUOTE BELOW 22.0 BPS HALF-WIDTH. Even the quietest setups can spike 5-10 bps without warning.

WORKED EXAMPLES WITH ACTUAL OUTCOMES

Example: change_5m = +3.68 bps, change_1m = -8.95 bps, tape = 0.765, 18:00 UTC, 360min to funding
- Regime: |change_5m| = 3.68 → mild = 28 bps base
- Time: 18:00 UTC → +7 bps
- Funding: 360min → +0 bps
- Tape: 0.765 last bar → +6 bps
- Recent move: |change_1m| = 8.95 → +0 bps (not extreme enough)
- Total: 28 + 7 + 6 = 41 bps
- Direction: recent -8.95 suggests retracement → delta +1 to +3 bps
- ACTUAL: moved -3.5 bps. A 41 bps spread captures this easily.

Example: change_5m = -46.18 bps, change_1m = -32.45 bps, tape = 0.558, 18:00 UTC, 360min to funding
- Regime: |change_5m| = 46.18 → high = 65 bps base
- Time: 18:00 UTC → +7 bps
- Funding: 360min → +0 bps
- Tape: 0.558 balanced → +0 bps
- Recent move: |change_1m| = 32.45 → +22 bps, and |change_5m| = 46.18 → +15 bps
- Total: 65 + 7 + 22 + 15 = 109 bps
- Direction: massive selloff suggests snapback but path chaotic → delta +5 to +15 bps
- ACTUAL: moved +23.6 bps. A 109 bps spread captures this; narrower quotes fail.

Example: change_5m = +41.84 bps, change_1m = -5.74 bps, tape = 0.586, 15:00 UTC, 60min to funding
- Regime: |change_5m| = 41.84 → high = 65 bps base
- Time: 15:00 UTC → +15 bps
- Funding: 60min → +18 bps
- Tape: 0.586 balanced → +0 bps
- Recent move: |change_5m| = 41.84 → +15 bps
- Total: 65 + 15 + 18 + 15 = 113 bps
- Direction: big 5m move but balanced tape suggests consolidation → delta -2 to +2 bps
- ACTUAL: moved +5.7 bps. A 113 bps spread captures this; 4.7 bps failed.

Example: change_5m = -3.18 bps, change_1m = -0.37 bps, tape = 0.23, 15:00 UTC, 60min to funding
- Regime: |change_5m| = 3.18 → mild = 28 bps base
- Time: 15:00 UTC → +15 bps
- Funding: 60min → +18 bps
- Tape: 0.23 last bar → +10 bps
- Total: 28 + 15 + 18 + 10 = 71 bps
- Direction: extreme selling tape suggests exhaustion → delta +1 to +3 bps
- ACTUAL: moved -8.1 bps. A 71 bps spread captures this; 1.6 bps failed catastrophically.

Example: change_5m = +3.46 bps, change_1m = +2.98 bps, tape = 0.844, 6:00 UTC, 120min to funding
- Regime: |change_5m| = 3.46 → mild = 28 bps base
- Time: 6:00 UTC → +9 bps
- Funding: 120min → +10 bps
- Tape: 0.844 last bar → +10 bps
- Total: 28 + 9 + 10 + 10 = 57 bps
- Direction: extreme buying spike suggests exhaustion → delta -1 to +1 bps
- ACTUAL: moved +1.3 bps. A 57 bps spread captures this; 2.4 bps succeeded narrowly.

THE MENTAL MODEL SHIFT

OLD (wrong): "It'll probably move 2 bps, so I quote ±3 bps to be safe"
NEW (correct): "The volatility regime is mild, it's 15:00 UTC with funding in 60 minutes, and the tape spiked, so I must quote at least 71 bps to contain the path, even though I expect only small movement"

You are quoting the range that will contain the realised path with high probability, NOT your best guess plus a small buffer.

DIRECTION SELECTION (after spread is set)

The spread protects you. Delta is secondary. Keep |delta_bps| modest.

1. After large recent move (|change_5m_bps| > 15 OR |change_1m_bps| > 8) without persistent driver → expect retracement
   - Quote delta opposite to the move direction, magnitude 0-4 bps depending on size
   - If |change_5m| > 50, consider larger retracement delta (5-12 bps) but widen spread accordingly

2. After extreme tape spike (>0.85 or <0.15) in last bar only → expect exhaustion
   - Quote delta opposite to the flow direction, magnitude 0-3 bps

3. After moderate move + now balanced tape → expect consolidation
   - Quote delta near 0, magnitude 0-2 bps

4. Sustained tape imbalance (3+ bars >0.65 or <0.35) with move continuing → cautiously continue
   - Quote delta with the flow, magnitude 1-4 bps

5. Funding <20 minutes → check perp basis if available, expect snapback toward spot
   - If basis visible and large, quote delta toward spot, magnitude 3-8 bps

6. US open hours (13:30-14:30 UTC) with volume surge → expect continuation of momentum
   - Quote delta with recent direction, magnitude 2-5 bps

7. Otherwise (conflicting signals, unclear regime) → quote delta 0 to ±1 bps

SCORING REALITY

Being inside your quote is everything. A wide quote with mediocre delta scores far better than a narrow quote that gets run over.

When in doubt: go wider, adjust delta conservatively toward zero or mean reversion, and ensure you capture the realised path.

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a confident forecast justifies acting. Most minutes should not be traded.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
